purpose: E3: the R6 corpora gain their first real consumers — the R3 learned-readability model evaluated on mutationbench_5000's REAL mutation outcomes via R3's own physics-verification method, and a per-policy behaviour evaluation streamed from replay_100k_ticks with no simulation.

replay_corpus_evaluation.statistic_note: the ranking uses the engine-faithful episode need_balance (full-horizon, post-death ticks as 0.0 — run_episode's own rule); the raw per-lived-tick mean is reported alongside because the two can DISAGREE when survival differs

decision.reason: Both corpora are consumed by real evaluations: the learned model scores 0.940625 pairwise accuracy on 2880 physics-labeled REAL mutation pairs (coverage 0.576 of 5000 — real mutations are rarely monotone, reported not hidden), and the stored replay corpus yields the per-policy behaviour comparison with zero simulation (switchboard ranks first on mean need balance). Verdicts are the numbers; both honest either way.

next_research_step: E4 (the slip module disposition) and E5 (the five player-notices audit); if the real-mutation accuracy is judged low, the bench's physics-labeled pairs are a ready fine-tuning corpus for the R3 trainer.
